name: Lightpanda Cloud

modes.label: Cloud headless browser
modes.note: Builder overage; Explorer has hard 10 hour monthly quota. Browser not Chromium; no pixel-perfect GUI guarantee. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee. Cloud serves the Lightpanda engine by default; browser=chrome runs Google Chrome for debugging only ('Chrome isn't intended for production traffic'). Metered by the second; concurrency overflow returns HTTP 429.

plans.name: Explorer
plans.note: 10 hours/month; BYOP; do not price unlimited usage at free tier.

plans.name: Builder
plans.note: 300 hours×$.08=$24 overage-equivalent included value; then $.08/hour. BYOP.

features.ip_note: Default fast_dc (single shared datacenter IP) or rotating shared datacenter pool with country; no residential offered, BYO proxy via console (Explorer and Builder).

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Resource-footprint and performance marketing comparisons are not CPU/RAM allocation guarantees. Compatibility is a CDP/WebAPI subset, not full Chrome desktop.
Builder concurrency 30 cannot fulfill 50 simultaneous browsers without Enterprise. Card preserves unknown resources null.

Cloud docs: metered by the second. CDP connection closes after 15 minutes regardless of quota; MCP idle timeout 5 minutes, active sessions can continue. Channel-specific cap cannot be represented by one max_session_h.

No graphics rendering pipeline: screenshot CDP returns a placeholder, not actual rendered page pixels. Local PNG/PDF output is text-only per README. This is not a screenshot-driven computer-use desktop substitute.

fleet.notes: Rendered pricing confirms 5/30. Browser sessions rather than generic VMs. 10 fits Builder; 50/300/1,000 need custom terms.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A CDP connection closes after 15 minutes, whatever your pool has left, so split long jobs across sessions.
snapshot_auto.note: Sessions are ephemeral browser sessions; no state save/restore documented. Hosted headless browser reached only over token-authenticated CDP / MCP (SSE) / HTTP fetch API; the customer gets no machine, shell, disk or exposed ports.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: CDP server ( serve ) Yes Yes MCP server Yes, all tools Partial, subset of tools AI agent Yes No fetch command Yes No HTTP API No Yes
snapshot_on_demand.note: Cloud interfaces are CDP, partial MCP and HTTP fetch only; no snapshot/checkpoint API. Cookies/storage live per session only.

harness_api.note: Feature-coverage table: built-in Lightpanda AI agent is Local=Yes, Cloud=No. Cloud MCP server (SSE) lets an external agent use the browser as a tool, which is not a harness API.

ingress_rules.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
ingress_rules.note: Not applicable: no user-exposed ports/URLs; the only way in is the token-authenticated CDP/MCP/API endpoint.

guest_firewall.note: No shell/root in a hosted browser session; nothing to run nftables in. Hosted headless browser reached only over token-authenticated CDP / MCP (SSE) / HTTP fetch API; the customer gets no machine, shell, disk or exposed ports.

secret_proxy.quote: Add your proxy on the proxies page in the console, then pass its identifier as the proxy parameter.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injection proxy for target sites. Only upstream-proxy credentials are stored console-side (referenced by id). Site credentials must be supplied by the client script (e.g. page.authenticate).

volume_attach.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
volume_attach.note: The customer gets a token-authenticated browser session (CDP/MCP/HTTP fetch), not a machine with attachable disks. No volumes/storage product is documented anywhere in the docs, pricing, or GitHub README; DuckDuckGo site search for volume/storage/persistent on lightpanda.io returns nothing.

volume_shared.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
volume_shared.note: Same reasoning as volume_attach: no persistent volume of any kind exists to share across sessions/machines. No storage/volume feature documented; outside what this headless-browser-as-a-service product is.

image_oci.quote: Use the cloud when you do not want to run or scale browsers. You sign up, get a token, and connect a remote browser with no process to manage and no host to keep alive.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Lightpanda Cloud provisions a managed browser session, not a machine you can boot from a custom image.

docker_inside.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — customers get a token-authenticated browser session (CDP/MCP/HTTP), not a machine to run containers on.

nested_virt.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shell/host access is exposed to run /dev/kvm workloads.

anti_bot.quote: Cloud serves the Lightpanda engine by default; browser=chrome runs Google Chrome for debugging only ('Chrome isn't intended for production traffic').
anti_bot.note: No stealth/fingerprint-evasion feature is documented on pricing, docs, or the proxy guide; only a managed upstream-proxy pool for IP rotation is offered.

captcha_solving.quote: Add your proxy on the proxies page in the console, then pass its identifier as the proxy parameter.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: no CAPTCHA-solving API/service is documented anywhere in the docs, pricing, or guides.

ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no machine/shell exposed, only CDP/MCP/HTTP browser endpoints.

snapshot.note: Cloud interfaces are CDP, partial MCP and HTTP fetch only; no snapshot/checkpoint API or disk is documented for sessions.

fork.note: not offered: no clone/fork-a-machine capability is documented; each session is a fresh browser instance opened over CDP/MCP/HTTP.

fork_running.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no fork capability of any kind is documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no fork/snapshot capability of any kind is documented.

pause_resume.quote: A CDP connection closes after 15 minutes, whatever your pool has left, so split long jobs across sessions.
pause_resume.note: Sessions are ephemeral and time out; no pause/resume of a running session is documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no persistent/sleeping machine to wake; a new session is opened per connection.

persistent_disk.quote: CDP server ( serve ) Yes Yes MCP server Yes, all tools Partial, subset of tools AI agent Yes No fetch command Yes No HTTP API No Yes
persistent_disk.note: not offered: no user-facing disk/filesystem is exposed for a hosted browser session; nothing documented survives across sessions.

auto_stop_idle.quote: A CDP connection closes after 15 minutes, whatever your pool has left, so split long jobs across sessions.
auto_stop_idle.note: Sessions are time/idle-bounded and closed automatically (15 min CDP cap; MCP idle timeout 5 minutes) rather than left running indefinitely.

live_resize.quote: Builder overage; Explorer has hard 10 hour monthly quota.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — browser sessions have no documented CPU/RAM sizing to resize; billing is per browser-hour, not per machine size.

agent_harnesses.note: The built-in Lightpanda AI agent is available locally but explicitly not available on Cloud per the feature-coverage table.

own_agent_api.note: Lightpanda's own built-in agent is Local-only (Yes) and Cloud=No; Cloud's MCP server lets an external agent use the browser as a tool, which is not the provider's own agent API.

lang_python.note: Docs nav lists a first-party Python SDK guide for driving Lightpanda (local and cloud).

lang_node.quote: import puppeteer from 'puppeteer-core'; const browser = await puppeteer.connect({ browserWSEndpoint: `wss://euwest.cloud.lightpanda.io/ws?token=${process.env.LPD_TOKEN}` });
lang_node.note: First-party Node.js (Puppeteer/Playwright via puppeteer-core/playwright-core) usage is documented as the primary connection method.

public_ipv4.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — customers get a shared wss:// endpoint, not a dedicated public IPv4 machine.

inbound_https.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no user-exposed ports/URLs; only the token-authenticated CDP/MCP/HTTP API endpoint is reachable.

egress_allowlist.quote: Add your proxy on the proxies page in the console, then pass its identifier as the proxy parameter.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: only a customer-supplied/managed outbound proxy pool is documented; no allow/deny-list or no-internet mode for egress is described.

egress_http_rules.quote: Add your proxy on the proxies page in the console, then pass its identifier as the proxy parameter.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no HTTP method/path-level egress rule feature is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Add your proxy on the proxies page in the console, then pass its identifier as the proxy parameter.
static_egress_ip.note: Default egress is a shared datacenter IP or rotating shared datacenter pool; a fixed dedicated outbound IP is not documented (only BYO proxy).

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Lightpanda Cloud is a headless browser service; no GPU machine type is offered.

windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Lightpanda Cloud runs on Linux servers only; no Windows machine option is documented.

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS option is documented; the product is a hosted Linux browser service.

hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no BAA/HIPAA-eligibility is documented for this small-team browser-automation product; no compliance page exists (/security, /trust return 404).

sso.quote: Sign up at console.lightpanda.io/signup. We'll email you a link to generate your API token.
sso.note: Onboarding is email/token based; no SAML/OIDC SSO is documented for the console.

eu_data_residency.note: An EU (west Europe) regional endpoint exists for choosing where the browser session runs, but no documentation guarantees data residency/storage restricted to that region.

max_session_h.quote: A CDP connection closes after 15 minutes, whatever your pool has left, so split long jobs across sessions.
max_session_h.note: CDP sessions are capped at 15 minutes (0.25h); MCP idle timeout is 5 minutes though active MCP sessions can continue longer. Channel-specific caps prevent one single precise number, but the documented CDP hard cap is used here.

arm64.quote: Lightpanda provides official Docker images for both Linux amd64 and arm64 architectures. ... Linux aarch64 is also available
arm64.note: Applies to the open-source engine/self-host artifacts (Linux aarch64 binaries, arm64 Docker images, aarch64-macos build); the managed Cloud product's own server CPU architecture is not published, but the product itself runs on/targets arm64.

soc2.quote: Enterprise ... Custom limits/volume, on-prem/private cloud, SLA.
soc2.note: No SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, or other compliance/security-attestation claim appears anywhere on the marketing site, docs, llms.txt/llms-full.txt, blog index, or pricing/Enterprise page (which lists SLA and on-prem but no compliance attestations); dedicated /security and /trust paths return 404. Small early-stage startup with no published attestation found.

desktop.quote: The headless browser built from scratch for AI agents and automation. Not a Chromium fork. Not a WebKit patch. A new browser, written in Zig.
desktop.note: Lightpanda is a headless-only browser engine with no rendering pipeline (per card caveats: screenshot CDP returns a placeholder, not real pixels) and no VNC/RDP/stream product. A graphical desktop is outside what this product is.

computer_use.quote: CDP server ( serve ) Yes Yes MCP server Yes, all tools Partial, subset of tools AI agent Yes No fetch command Yes No HTTP API No Yes
computer_use.note: Cloud interfaces are CDP / partial MCP / HTTP fetch only, driving the headless DOM, not a screenshot+click computer-use API; no rendered pixels exist to click on (screenshot CDP is a placeholder). Outside what this headless-browser product is.

isolation.quote: Scripts run in an isolated container.
isolation.note: Documented for the Cloud console's Playground script-runner (also read-only filesystem except /tmp, 256MB RAM, 1 CPU core, capped processes). No separate statement covers isolation of the underlying browser-session process itself (reached over CDP/MCP/HTTP), but Lightpanda Cloud has no VM/microVM product surface (no ssh, no custom images, no root) consistent with a container-based multi-tenant backend; taken as the best available evidence for the whole product's isolation model.
